samples.name: csv_query
samples.description: loads a CSV file, builds an index over one column, and answers point queries efficiently
samples.entry_signature: def csv_query_main(csv_path: str, column: str, key: str) -> None:
steps: Read a CSV file from a given path and return its rows as a list of dictionaries.
Build a dictionary that maps each unique value in a chosen column to the list of rows that contain it.
Given a key, return the matching rows from the index in O(1) lookup, or an empty list if the key is absent.
Read a CSV path, a column name, and a query key from the command line, then print the matching rows.

samples.name: top_k_words
samples.description: reports the K most frequent words in a text file
samples.entry_signature: def top_k_words_main(path: str, k: int) -> None:
steps: Read a text file from a given path and return its contents as a single string.
Tokenize a string into a list of lowercase words, stripping surrounding punctuation.
Count the occurrences of each word and return a dictionary mapping word to count.
Return the top-K words sorted by descending count, breaking ties alphabetically.
Read a file path and K from the command line, then print each top word with its count.

samples.name: maze_bfs
samples.description: finds the shortest path through a 2D grid maze using BFS
samples.entry_signature: def solve_maze(maze: list[str]) -> str:
steps: Parse a maze from a list of strings where '#' is a wall, '.' is open, 'S' is the start, and 'G' is the goal; return a 2D grid along with the start and goal coordinates.
Run breadth-first search from the start cell and return a parent map that records, for each visited cell, the cell it was first reached from.
Reconstruct the path from the start to the goal using the parent map, returning an empty list if the goal is unreachable.
Render the maze as a single string with the path cells marked by '*'.

samples.name: game_of_life
samples.description: simulates Conway's Game of Life for a bounded number of generations
samples.entry_signature: def run_life(initial: list[str], max_generations: int) -> list[str]:
steps: Parse an initial grid from a list of strings where 'O' marks an alive cell and '.' marks a dead one.
Given a grid, compute the next generation by applying Conway's rules to every cell.
Detect whether the simulation has reached a stable state by comparing the current grid to the previous one.
Run the simulation for at most max_generations, stopping early if a stable state is reached; return the final grid as a list of strings.

samples.name: ascii_histogram
samples.description: reads numbers from a file and prints an ASCII bar chart of their distribution
samples.entry_signature: def histogram_main(path: str, n_bins: int) -> None:
steps: Read a file of one number per line and return a list of floats.
Bucket the numbers into n_bins equal-width bins between the min and max value, and return a list of counts per bin.
Format the counts as ASCII bars where each '#' represents a fixed number of items.
Read a file path and n_bins from the command line, then print the histogram.

samples.name: markdown_outline
samples.description: extracts a nested outline of headings from a Markdown document
samples.entry_signature: def outline_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a Markdown file from a given path and return its contents as a single string.
Find every heading line and return a list of (level, text) tuples, where level is the number of leading '#' characters.
Format the headings as an indented outline, using two spaces of indent per level above 1.
Read a file path from the command line and print the formatted outline.

samples.name: inventory_report
samples.description: scans an inventory CSV and flags low-stock and soon-to-expire items
samples.entry_signature: def inventory_report_main(csv_path: str, low_stock_threshold: int, expiry_days: int, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Load an inventory CSV with columns (name, quantity, expiry_date) into a list of dictionaries.
Filter the items whose quantity is below a given threshold and return the filtered list.
Filter the items whose expiry_date falls within the next N days from today and return the filtered list.
Write a Markdown report with two sections, 'Low stock' and 'Expiring soon', listing the affected items.

samples.name: expr_calc
samples.description: evaluates arithmetic expressions over integers using the shunting-yard algorithm
samples.entry_signature: def calc_main() -> None:
steps: Tokenize an input string into a list of integers, operators ('+', '-', '*', '/'), and parentheses.
Convert an infix token list to Reverse Polish Notation using the shunting-yard algorithm.
Evaluate an RPN token list and return the integer result.
Read expressions from standard input one per line, evaluate each, and print the result.

samples.name: k_means
samples.description: runs K-means clustering on a list of 2D points
samples.entry_signature: def k_means(points: list[tuple[float, float]], k: int, max_iter: int) -> tuple[list[tuple[float, float]], list[int]]:
steps: Initialize K cluster centers by sampling K points from the input uniformly at random without replacement.
Assign each point to the index of the nearest cluster center under Euclidean distance and return the assignment list.
Recompute each cluster center as the mean of the points currently assigned to it.
Iterate the assignment and re-centering steps until the assignments stop changing or max_iter is reached, then return the final centers and assignments.

samples.name: log_summary
samples.description: parses a server log file and reports error counts by hour
samples.entry_signature: def log_summary_main(log_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a log file whose lines have the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL message' and return a list of dictionaries with the parsed fields.
Filter the entries whose LEVEL is 'ERROR' and return the filtered list.
Group the error entries by hour ('YYYY-MM-DD HH') and return a dictionary mapping each hour to its error count.
Read a log path from the command line and print the grouped counts in chronological order, one line per hour.

samples.name: json_dedupe
samples.description: deduplicates JSONL records by keeping the most recent per key
samples.entry_signature: def json_dedupe_main(in_path: str, out_path: str, key_field: str, timestamp_field: str) -> None:
steps: Read a JSONL file and return its records as a list of dictionaries.
Group the records by the given key field, returning a dictionary from key value to list of records.
For each group, select the record whose timestamp field is the most recent.
Write the selected records to an output file in JSONL format.

samples.name: sales_summary
samples.description: computes monthly sales totals from a transactions CSV
samples.entry_signature: def sales_summary_main(csv_path: str) -> None:
steps: Load a CSV of transactions with columns (date, customer, amount) into a list of dictionaries.
Parse each date string into a 'YYYY-MM' bucket.
Sum the amount per bucket and return a dictionary mapping bucket to total.
Print the buckets in chronological order along with their totals.

samples.name: csv_to_json_grouped
samples.description: converts a CSV to a JSON file grouped by one key column
samples.entry_signature: def csv_to_json_main(csv_path: str, json_path: str, key_column: str) -> None:
steps: Read the CSV file into a list of row dictionaries.
Group the rows by the value of the chosen key column.
Drop the key column from each grouped record so only the remaining fields remain.
Write the grouped result to the output JSON file.

samples.name: dedupe_emails
samples.description: cleans a list of email addresses, dropping invalid and duplicate entries
samples.entry_signature: def dedupe_emails_main(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read email addresses from a file, one per line, into a list of strings.
Normalize each address by lowercasing it and stripping surrounding whitespace.
Discard addresses that do not contain both an '@' character and a '.' character.
Write the remaining unique addresses to a new file in sorted order.

samples.name: csv_join
samples.description: joins two CSV files on a shared column
samples.entry_signature: def csv_join_main(left_path: str, right_path: str, join_column: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read both CSV files into lists of row dictionaries.
Build a lookup dictionary from the right file keyed by the join column.
For each row of the left file, merge in the matching row from the lookup if present.
Write the merged rows to the output CSV with the union of all columns.

samples.name: outlier_filter
samples.description: removes CSV rows whose numeric column is far from the column mean
samples.entry_signature: def outlier_filter_main(in_path: str, out_path: str, column: str, k_sigma: float) -> None:
steps: Load a CSV into a list of row dictionaries.
Compute the mean and standard deviation of a chosen numeric column.
Keep only rows whose value in that column falls within k_sigma standard deviations of the mean.
Write the kept rows to a new CSV file.

samples.name: sqlite_export
samples.description: exports an SQLite table to CSV
samples.entry_signature: def sqlite_export_main(db_path: str, table: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Connect to an SQLite database file at the given path.
Read all rows from the chosen table along with the column names.
Format each row as a comma-separated string with proper quoting of values containing commas or quotes.
Write the header row followed by all data rows to a CSV file.

samples.name: rolling_average
samples.description: computes a rolling average of one numeric column of a CSV
samples.entry_signature: def rolling_average_main(in_path: str, out_path: str, column: str, window: int) -> None:
steps: Read a CSV file, preserving the order of rows, into a list of dictionaries.
For each row index, collect the values of the chosen column for the previous window rows including the current row.
Compute the mean of each window and attach it to the corresponding row under a new key.
Write all rows with the new column to an output CSV file.

samples.name: pivot_table
samples.description: builds a pivot table from a CSV by summing a value column
samples.entry_signature: def pivot_table_main(csv_path: str, row_col: str, col_col: str, val_col: str) -> None:
steps: Load the CSV into a list of row dictionaries.
Build a nested dictionary keyed by row value then column value with the sum of val_col as the entry.
Convert the nested dictionary into a 2D matrix using sorted row keys and sorted column keys.
Print the pivot table as an aligned grid with the header row and the key column.

samples.name: bucket_partition
samples.description: partitions a JSON dataset into separate files by year-month
samples.entry_signature: def bucket_partition_main(in_path: str, out_dir: str, date_field: str) -> None:
steps: Read the records from the input JSON file into a list of dictionaries.
For each record, compute its 'YYYY-MM' bucket from the date_field value.
Group records by their bucket into a dictionary mapping bucket name to a list of records.
For each bucket, write the records to a file named after the bucket inside out_dir.

samples.name: schema_check
samples.description: validates that a CSV conforms to a required-columns schema
samples.entry_signature: def schema_check_main(csv_path: str, required: list[str]) -> None:
steps: Read the CSV file and capture the header along with all rows.
Check that every column in the required list appears in the header; report any missing columns.
For each row, collect every (row_index, column, reason) violation where a required column is missing or empty.
Print the count of valid rows along with the list of violations.

samples.name: api_paginator
samples.description: walks a paginated mock-API source and gathers all items
samples.entry_signature: def paginate_main() -> None:
steps: Define a function get_page(cursor) that returns a fixed mock response with an items list and a next_cursor (or None).
Repeatedly call get_page starting with a None cursor, accumulating all items until next_cursor is None.
Deduplicate the accumulated items by their 'id' field, keeping the first occurrence.
Print the total item count and the first three deduplicated items.

samples.name: csv_normalize
samples.description: normalizes the numeric columns of a CSV into the [0, 1] range
samples.entry_signature: def csv_normalize_main(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Load the CSV into a list of row dictionaries.
Identify the numeric columns by checking that every value in the column parses as a float.
For each numeric column, rescale every value to the [0, 1] range using the column's min and max.
Write the normalized rows to a new CSV file.

samples.name: dependency_resolver
samples.description: topologically sorts tasks given pairwise dependencies
samples.entry_signature: def deps_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read (task, dependency) pairs from the file, one per line, separated by whitespace.
Build a directed dependency graph as an adjacency list from task to its dependents.
Run Kahn's algorithm to obtain a topological order, detecting any cycle.
Print the linear ordering if one exists, or report the nodes involved in the cycle.

samples.name: dir_inventory
samples.description: summarizes file sizes in a directory tree by extension
samples.entry_signature: def dir_inventory_main(root: str) -> None:
steps: Walk the directory tree starting at the given root.
For each file encountered, record its size in bytes and its extension.
Aggregate the total size and file count per extension into a summary dictionary.
Print the summary sorted by total size in descending order, with a human-readable size format.

samples.name: csv_columns_rename
samples.description: renames CSV columns according to a mapping file
samples.entry_signature: def csv_rename_main(in_path: str, out_path: str, mapping_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the mapping file as a JSON dictionary from old column names to new column names.
Load the input CSV header and rows.
Apply the mapping to the header, keeping any column not present in the mapping unchanged.
Write the renamed header and the unchanged rows to an output CSV.

samples.name: merge_csv_files
samples.description: merges multiple CSV files with the same header into one
samples.entry_signature: def merge_csv_main(in_paths: list[str], out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the header of the first input file and treat it as the canonical header.
For each input file in order, verify that its header matches the canonical one.
Stream the data rows of every input file into a single combined list.
Write the canonical header followed by all data rows to the output file.

samples.name: html_strip
samples.description: strips HTML tags from a document and collapses whitespace
samples.entry_signature: def html_strip_main(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the HTML file at the given path into a single string.
Scan the string and remove every substring that begins with '<' and ends with the next '>'.
Collapse runs of whitespace in the result into single spaces and strip the ends.
Write the cleaned text to the output path.

samples.name: ngram_freq
samples.description: counts character n-grams of a fixed length in a text file
samples.entry_signature: def ngram_main(path: str, n: int, k: int) -> None:
steps: Read the text file at the given path into a single string.
Iterate over the string and extract every contiguous substring of length n.
Count the occurrences of each n-gram and store the counts in a dictionary.
Print the K most frequent n-grams sorted by descending count.

samples.name: anagram_groups
samples.description: groups words from a file that are anagrams of each other
samples.entry_signature: def anagram_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read words from the file, one per line, into a list of strings.
Compute a normalized key for each word by sorting its lowercase letters.
Group words sharing the same normalized key into a dictionary mapping key to list of words.
Print every group whose size is greater than one.

samples.name: regex_extract
samples.description: extracts every match of a regex from a text file
samples.entry_signature: def regex_extract_main(path: str, pattern: str) -> None:
steps: Read a regex pattern and a file path from the command line.
Read the file contents as a single string.
Find every non-overlapping match of the pattern in the string.
Print each match on its own line in the order found.

samples.name: diff_lines
samples.description: shows a line-level diff between two text files
samples.entry_signature: def diff_main(left_path: str, right_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read both files into lists of lines, preserving order.
Compute the set of lines present in the left file but not the right.
Compute the set of lines present in the right file but not the left.
Print the deletions prefixed with '-' and additions prefixed with '+'.

samples.name: edit_distance
samples.description: computes the Levenshtein distance between two strings
samples.entry_signature: def edit_distance_main(a: str, b: str) -> None:
steps: Read two strings a and b from the command line.
Build a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] is the edit distance between the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b.
Fill the table using the standard insert / delete / replace recurrence.
Print the final distance and the full DP table.

samples.name: palindrome_finder
samples.description: finds palindromic substrings of length at least L in a string
samples.entry_signature: def palindromes_main(s: str, min_len: int) -> None:
steps: Read a string and a minimum length from the command line.
Iterate over every contiguous substring of length at least min_len.
Check whether each substring reads the same forwards and backwards.
Print the unique palindromes in descending order of length, breaking ties alphabetically.

samples.name: paragraph_summary
samples.description: picks the K most representative sentences from a text by word overlap
samples.entry_signature: def summary_main(path: str, k: int) -> None:
steps: Read the text file into a single string.
Split the string into sentences using punctuation as a delimiter.
For each sentence, compute a score equal to the sum of word-overlap counts with every other sentence.
Print the top-K sentences by score in the order they appeared in the text.

samples.name: acronym_expander
samples.description: expands acronyms in a text using a JSON glossary
samples.entry_signature: def acronym_main(text_path: str, glossary_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the glossary JSON file as a dictionary mapping acronyms to their full forms.
Read the target text file into a single string.
For each acronym in the glossary, replace whole-word occurrences with 'acronym (full form)'.
Write the expanded text to the output file.

samples.name: slugify
samples.description: converts each line of text in a file into a URL-friendly slug
samples.entry_signature: def slugify_main(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the input file into a list of lines, stripping trailing newlines.
For each line, lowercase it and replace any non-alphanumeric character with a hyphen.
Collapse runs of consecutive hyphens into one and strip leading and trailing hyphens.
Write the resulting slugs to the output file, one per line.

samples.name: typo_correct
samples.description: suggests corrections for misspelled words against a dictionary
samples.entry_signature: def typo_main(dict_path: str, input_path: str) -> None:
steps: Load a dictionary of valid words from a file into a set.
Load the input words to correct from another file as a list.
For each input word not in the dictionary, find the dictionary word with the smallest edit distance.
Print each input word followed by its best correction.

samples.name: rhyme_groups
samples.description: groups words by their last K letters
samples.entry_signature: def rhyme_main(path: str, k: int) -> None:
steps: Read words from a file, one per line, into a list.
For each word, compute a key equal to its last K letters in lowercase.
Group words sharing the same key into a dictionary from key to word list.
Print every group whose size is greater than one in alphabetical order of the key.

samples.name: tag_stripper
samples.description: removes hashtags and mentions from social-media text
samples.entry_signature: def tag_strip_main(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the input file into a list of lines, treating one line as one post.
For each line, split it on whitespace and drop any token that starts with '#' or '@'.
Rejoin the remaining tokens with a single space and strip the ends.
Write the cleaned lines to the output file.

samples.name: email_header_parse
samples.description: parses simple RFC-2822-style email headers from a file
samples.entry_signature: def email_parse_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the email file at the given path into a single string.
Split the string at the first blank line into a header section and a body section.
Parse the header section into a dictionary mapping field names to their string values.
Print the parsed header dictionary and the length of the body.

samples.name: caesar_cipher
samples.description: encrypts and decrypts text with a Caesar shift
samples.entry_signature: def caesar_main(text: str, shift: int) -> None:
steps: Read a string and a shift integer from the command line.
Shift every alphabetic character by the given amount, preserving case and wrapping around.
Leave non-alphabetic characters unchanged in the output.
Print the encrypted text and verify by decrypting it back to the original.

samples.name: stopword_filter
samples.description: removes stopwords from a text using a stopword list
samples.entry_signature: def stopword_main(text_path: str, stopword_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the stopword list from a file into a set of lowercase words.
Read the input text file into a single string.
Tokenize the string into words and discard any token that, when lowercased, is in the stopword set.
Write the remaining tokens, joined by single spaces, to the output file.

samples.name: dijkstra
samples.description: computes shortest paths from a source in a weighted directed graph
samples.entry_signature: def dijkstra_main(edge_path: str, source: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the edge file of (u, v, w) entries into an adjacency list of (neighbor, weight) pairs.
Initialize a distances dictionary with infinity for every node and 0 for the source.
Use a min-heap to repeatedly extract the closest unsettled node and relax each outgoing edge.
Print the final shortest distance from the source to every node, sorted by node name.

samples.name: knapsack_01
samples.description: solves the 0/1 knapsack problem with dynamic programming
samples.entry_signature: def knapsack_main(items_path: str, capacity: int) -> None:
steps: Read item weights and values from a file into two parallel lists of integers.
Build a 2D DP table indexed by item count and remaining capacity, initialized to zero.
Fill the table using the take-or-skip recurrence for each item.
Print the maximum achievable value and the indices of the items chosen.

samples.name: mergesort
samples.description: sorts a list of integers using merge sort
samples.entry_signature: def mergesort_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a list of integers from a file, one per line.
Implement a function merge(left, right) that combines two already-sorted lists into a single sorted list.
Implement a recursive sort that splits the list in halves and merges the sorted halves.
Print the resulting sorted list.

samples.name: lcs
samples.description: finds the longest common subsequence of two strings
samples.entry_signature: def lcs_main(a: str, b: str) -> None:
steps: Read two strings a and b from the command line.
Build a 2D DP table of common-subsequence lengths over the prefixes of a and b.
Backtrack through the DP table to reconstruct one longest common subsequence.
Print the LCS string and its length.

samples.name: n_queens
samples.description: finds one solution to the N-queens problem
samples.entry_signature: def n_queens_main(n: int) -> None:
steps: Read N from the command line.
Recursively place a queen on each row, tracking columns and diagonals already used.
Backtrack when no safe column is available in the current row.
Print one valid board as an N×N grid using 'Q' and '.' characters.

samples.name: subset_sum
samples.description: finds a subset of integers that sums to a target
samples.entry_signature: def subset_sum_main(path: str, target: int) -> None:
steps: Read a list of integers and a target sum from a file.
Recursively explore including or excluding each integer, caching results by (index, remaining).
Reconstruct the chosen subset from the cache when a solution is found.
Print the subset, or 'no solution' if no subset reaches the target.

samples.name: edit_path_trace
samples.description: reconstructs the edit operations between two strings
samples.entry_signature: def edit_path_main(a: str, b: str) -> None:
steps: Read two strings a and b from the command line.
Build the standard edit-distance DP table for the two strings.
Backtrack through the table to derive an ordered sequence of insert / delete / replace operations.
Print each operation in order along with the running state of the transformed string.

samples.name: union_find
samples.description: groups elements by merging them with union-find
samples.entry_signature: def union_find_main(merge_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read pairs (a, b) to be merged from a file, one pair per line.
Maintain a union-find data structure with path compression and union by rank.
Apply each merge using the data structure.
Print the group representative for every element in sorted order.

samples.name: interval_scheduling
samples.description: selects the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals
samples.entry_signature: def interval_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read (start, end) interval pairs from a file, one per line.
Sort the intervals by their end time in ascending order.
Greedily pick each interval whose start is not earlier than the previous pick's end.
Print the chosen intervals in the order they were picked.

samples.name: trie_prefix
samples.description: builds a prefix trie and answers prefix queries
samples.entry_signature: def trie_main(dict_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a list of words from a file, one per line.
Insert each word into a trie data structure built from nested dictionaries.
Implement a search function that returns all words sharing a given prefix.
Read prefixes from standard input one per line and print the matching words for each.

samples.name: rod_cutting
samples.description: maximizes revenue from cutting a rod into pieces
samples.entry_signature: def rod_main(prices_path: str, length: int) -> None:
steps: Read a list of prices indexed by piece length from a file.
Build a 1D DP table indexed by length, initialized to zero.
Fill the table using the cut-or-keep recurrence.
Print the optimal revenue along with one cutting plan that achieves it.

samples.name: graph_components
samples.description: counts and labels connected components in an undirected graph
samples.entry_signature: def components_main(edge_path: str) -> None:
steps: Parse edges from a file into an undirected adjacency list.
Run depth-first search starting at each unvisited node, assigning a component label as you go.
Track the size of each component while traversing.
Print the number of components and the size of each one.

samples.name: rotated_binary_search
samples.description: searches for a value in a rotated sorted array
samples.entry_signature: def rotated_search_main(path: str, target: int) -> None:
steps: Read a rotated sorted list of integers and a target value from a file.
Find the rotation pivot using a binary search variant.
Run a second binary search in the half of the array that contains the target.
Print the index of the target or -1 if it is absent.

samples.name: sudoku_validator
samples.description: checks whether a 9x9 Sudoku grid is valid
samples.entry_signature: def sudoku_main(grid_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the grid from a file as nine rows of nine digits, with '0' representing a blank cell.
Verify that each row contains no repeated non-zero digit, collecting any violations.
Verify the same property for each column and each 3x3 block.
Print 'valid' if no violations exist, or list every violation found.

samples.name: rabin_karp
samples.description: finds every match of a pattern in a text using rolling hashes
samples.entry_signature: def rabin_karp_main(text_path: str, pattern: str) -> None:
steps: Read the text from a file as a single string.
Compute the rolling hash of the pattern and the first window of the text.
Slide the window across the text, updating the hash and comparing it to the pattern hash.
Verify each hash match by direct string comparison and print every confirmed match index.

samples.name: topological_layers
samples.description: decomposes a DAG into longest-path layers
samples.entry_signature: def layers_main(edge_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the DAG edges from a file into an adjacency list.
Compute the in-degree of every node and identify the sources.
Repeatedly remove the current set of sources as a layer, decrementing in-degrees as you go.
Print each layer on its own line in order.

samples.name: bouncing_ball
samples.description: simulates a 1D bouncing ball with damping
samples.entry_signature: def bouncing_ball_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read the initial height, gravity, damping coefficient, and time step from a config file.
Loop in fixed time steps, updating the velocity and position of the ball.
Detect each ground contact and apply the damping coefficient to the reflected velocity.
Print time, height, and velocity at every step until the ball's energy falls below a tolerance.

samples.name: predator_prey
samples.description: simulates a discrete-time Lotka-Volterra system
samples.entry_signature: def lotka_main(path: str, steps: int) -> None:
steps: Read the initial populations and the four model parameters from a config file.
For each time step, compute the change in prey and predator populations from the equations.
Update the populations and append the new values to time-series lists.
Print the populations at every step up to the given step count.

samples.name: traffic_grid
samples.description: advances a cellular traffic-flow model on a 1D road
samples.entry_signature: def traffic_main(road: str, steps: int) -> None:
steps: Parse the road as a list of characters where '#' is a car and '.' is empty.
For each step, move every car forward by one position if the next cell is empty, updating in lock-step.
Detect whether the road has reached a steady state by comparing the current state with the previous one.
Print the road at each step until steady state or the step limit is reached.

samples.name: percolation
samples.description: determines whether a random grid percolates from top to bottom
samples.entry_signature: def percolation_main(rows: int, cols: int, p: float) -> None:
steps: Initialize a grid of the given dimensions, opening each cell independently with probability p.
Run a flood fill from every cell in the top row to mark cells connected to the top.
Determine whether any cell in the bottom row was reached by the flood fill.
Print whether the grid percolates and render the grid with reached cells marked.

samples.name: forest_fire
samples.description: advances a forest-fire cellular automaton until the fire dies out
samples.entry_signature: def fire_main(initial: list[str]) -> None:
steps: Parse the initial grid into a 2D list where each cell is 'T' (tree), 'F' (fire), or '.' (empty).
For each step, apply the rules: trees adjacent to fire ignite, fires turn empty, empty cells stay empty.
Count the number of trees, fires, and empty cells after each step.
Print the grid and the counts at each step until no fires remain.

samples.name: mm1_queue
samples.description: simulates an M/M/1 queue with Poisson arrivals
samples.entry_signature: def mm1_main(arrival_rate: float, service_rate: float, total_time: float) -> None:
steps: Sample arrival times using exponentially distributed inter-arrival intervals up to total_time.
Sample service times for each arrival from an exponential distribution.
Process arrivals and departures in chronological order, updating the queue length and waiting times.
Print the mean waiting time and the maximum queue length observed.

samples.name: random_walk_2d
samples.description: simulates a 2D random walk on a lattice
samples.entry_signature: def walk_main(steps: int) -> None:
steps: Read the number of steps from the command line.
At each step, pick a random cardinal direction and update the current position.
Record the trajectory of positions as a list of (x, y) tuples.
Print the start, the end, and the maximum distance reached from the origin.

samples.name: sir_epidemic
samples.description: runs a deterministic SIR epidemic simulation
samples.entry_signature: def sir_main(pop: int, init_infected: int, beta: float, gamma: float) -> None:
steps: Initialize the susceptible, infected, and recovered counts from the population and initial infected.
For each day, compute new infections and new recoveries from the current counts and the rates.
Update the S, I, and R counts and append them to a daily time series.
Print the daily counts until the infected count reaches zero.

samples.name: boids_step
samples.description: advances a flock of Boids with alignment, cohesion, and separation
samples.entry_signature: def boids_main(n_agents: int, n_steps: int) -> None:
steps: Initialize n_agents with random 2D positions and small random velocities.
For each agent, compute the alignment, cohesion, and separation vectors from agents within a fixed radius.
Update each agent's velocity by combining the three vectors and clamping its speed.
Print the final positions of every agent after n_steps.

samples.name: brownian_box
samples.description: simulates Brownian motion of N particles inside a square box
samples.entry_signature: def brownian_main(n_particles: int, n_steps: int, box: float) -> None:
steps: Initialize the particles at random positions uniformly inside the box.
At each step, perturb every particle's position with independent Gaussian noise.
Reflect any particle that crosses a wall back into the box.
Print the final positions of all particles after n_steps.

samples.name: elevator_dispatch
samples.description: dispatches an elevator through a queue of pickup-and-drop requests
samples.entry_signature: def elevator_main(requests_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read (time, source_floor, target_floor) requests from a file, one per line.
Maintain the elevator's current floor and a sorted queue of pending requests.
Tick the simulation forward one floor at a time, picking up and dropping off requests on the way.
Print each request along with the time at which it was completed.

samples.name: logistic_map
samples.description: iterates the logistic map and labels the resulting regime
samples.entry_signature: def logistic_main(r: float, x0: float, n_steps: int) -> None:
steps: Read r, x0, and n_steps from the command line.
Iterate x_{n+1} = r * x_n * (1 - x_n) for n_steps steps, recording every value.
Inspect the tail of the sequence and label it as fixed, periodic, or chaotic.
Print the regime label and the last few values of the sequence.

samples.name: drunkard_walk_home
samples.description: runs a random walk until the walker reaches home or gives up
samples.entry_signature: def drunkard_main(start: tuple[int, int], home: tuple[int, int], max_steps: int) -> None:
steps: Read the start and home coordinates and the step cap from a config.
Step the walker one unit in a random cardinal direction each tick.
Stop when the walker reaches the home location or when the step cap is exceeded.
Print whether home was reached and the number of steps taken.

samples.name: flu_in_school
samples.description: spreads an infection day-by-day across a friendship roster
samples.entry_signature: def flu_main(roster_path: str, seed_student: str, prob: float) -> None:
steps: Read a JSON roster mapping each student to their list of friends.
Initialize the infection state with one infected student (the seed).
For each day, infect each susceptible friend of an infected student with the given probability.
Print the cumulative number of infected students at the end of each day until no new infections occur.

samples.name: rumor_spread
samples.description: spreads a rumor over a friendship graph
samples.entry_signature: def rumor_main(graph_path: str, seed: str, prob: float, max_steps: int) -> None:
steps: Read the JSON graph mapping each person to their list of friends.
Mark the seed person as informed and everyone else as uninformed.
At each step, every informed person tells each of their friends with the given probability.
Print the number of informed people after every step until everyone knows or the step cap is hit.

samples.name: growth_colony
samples.description: grows a bacterial colony from a single cell on a 2D grid
samples.entry_signature: def colony_main(rows: int, cols: int, max_steps: int) -> None:
steps: Initialize a grid of the given dimensions with a single bacterium at the center.
For each step, every bacterium attempts to spawn into a random empty 4-neighbour cell.
Apply all spawns in lock-step using a working copy of the grid.
Print the grid and the colony size after each step until full coverage or the step cap.

samples.name: dice_pool
samples.description: samples the success-count distribution of a dice pool
samples.entry_signature: def dice_main(n_dice: int, threshold: int, trials: int) -> None:
steps: Read the number of dice, the success threshold, and the trial count from the command line.
For each trial, roll n_dice six-sided dice and count how many meet the success threshold.
Tally the success counts across all trials.
Print the empirical probability of each success count, sorted by success count.

samples.name: file_search_cli
samples.description: recursively searches for filenames matching a glob pattern
samples.entry_signature: def file_search_main(root: str, pattern: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the root directory and the glob pattern from command-line arguments.
Walk the directory tree starting at the root using os.walk.
For each file encountered, check whether its name matches the pattern using fnmatch.
Print each matching path on its own line.

samples.name: csv_head_tail
samples.description: prints the first and last N rows of a CSV file
samples.entry_signature: def head_tail_main(csv_path: str, n: int) -> None:
steps: Parse the file path and N from command-line arguments.
Read the CSV header and the full list of data rows.
Slice out the first N rows and the last N rows.
Print the header, the first slice, an ellipsis line, and the last slice.

samples.name: batch_rename
samples.description: renames every file in a directory by applying a regex substitution
samples.entry_signature: def rename_main(directory: str, pattern: str, replacement: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the directory path, the regex pattern, and the replacement string from arguments.
List every file in the directory.
Compute each file's new name by applying the regex substitution to the old name.
Rename each file and print the old and new names side by side.

samples.name: uptime_monitor
samples.description: checks a list of URLs for reachability and prints a report
samples.entry_signature: def uptime_main(urls_path: str, timeout: float) -> None:
steps: Parse a URL-list file path and a timeout from command-line arguments.
Read the URLs from the file, one per line.
For each URL, perform a mocked reachability check returning a (reachable, latency_ms) pair.
Print a table of URL, status, and latency, sorted by ascending latency.

samples.name: archive_extract
samples.description: extracts a tar or zip archive to a destination directory
samples.entry_signature: def extract_main(archive_path: str, dest_dir: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the archive path and the destination directory from arguments.
Determine whether the archive is a .tar or .zip based on its file extension.
Extract every member of the archive into the destination, preserving the directory structure.
Print each extracted path and the total number of extracted files.

samples.name: csv_filter_cli
samples.description: filters rows of a CSV file according to a column predicate
samples.entry_signature: def csv_filter_main(csv_path: str, column: str, predicate: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the CSV path, the column name, and a predicate expression from arguments.
Load the CSV into a list of row dictionaries.
Evaluate the predicate against the chosen column value for each row, keeping only those where it is true.
Print the filtered rows in CSV format with the original header.

samples.name: timer_repl
samples.description: runs an interactive REPL that times each user-entered snippet
samples.entry_signature: def timer_repl_main() -> None:
steps: Read snippets from standard input one per line until EOF.
For each snippet, execute it in an isolated namespace while measuring the elapsed wall time.
Catch and capture any exception with a short error message.
Print the snippet, the elapsed time, and the result or error per line.

samples.name: du_summary
samples.description: prints disk usage of a directory's immediate children
samples.entry_signature: def du_main(root: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the root directory from the command line.
List the immediate children (files and subdirectories) of the root.
For each child, compute the total recursive byte size in bytes.
Print each child and its size in a human-readable format, sorted by descending size.

samples.name: tail_follow
samples.description: polls a log file and prints any newly appended lines
samples.entry_signature: def tail_follow_main(path: str, poll_interval: float, max_polls: int) -> None:
steps: Parse the file path, poll interval, and maximum number of polls from arguments.
Open the file and seek to its current end.
Loop, reading any newly appended lines and printing them between sleeps of poll_interval.
Stop after max_polls iterations or when the file is detected as truncated.

samples.name: ip_lookup_cli
samples.description: resolves a list of hostnames to IP addresses
samples.entry_signature: def ip_lookup_main(hosts_path: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the host-list file path from the command line.
Read the hostnames from the file, one per line.
For each hostname, perform a mocked DNS lookup returning either an IP address or an error string.
Print a table of hostname, IP, and status.

samples.name: csv_groupby_cli
samples.description: groups a CSV by a column and prints aggregate statistics
samples.entry_signature: def csv_groupby_main(csv_path: str, group_col: str, value_col: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the CSV path, the group-by column, and the value column from arguments.
Load the CSV into row dictionaries.
Group the rows by the group column and accumulate the value column inside each group.
Print each group's key, count, sum, and mean, sorted by descending sum.

samples.name: password_check_cli
samples.description: audits a list of passwords against simple strength rules
samples.entry_signature: def password_check_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read passwords from a file, one per line.
For each password, check rules: minimum length, presence of a digit, an uppercase letter, and a symbol.
Compute a score between 0 and 4 from the number of rules passed.
Print each password along with its score and the names of any failing rules.

samples.name: csv_to_markdown
samples.description: converts a CSV file into a Markdown table
samples.entry_signature: def csv_md_main(csv_path: str) -> None:
steps: Parse the CSV path from the command line.
Load the header and the rows of the CSV.
Compute the maximum width for each column and pad each cell to that width.
Print the Markdown header, the separator row, and the data rows.

samples.name: port_scan_mock
samples.description: runs a mocked port scan over a host's port range
samples.entry_signature: def port_scan_main(host: str, start: int, end: int) -> None:
steps: Parse the host and the inclusive port range from command-line arguments.
For each port, perform a mocked connection check that returns open or closed.
Collect the open ports into a sorted list.
Print every open port along with a guessed service name from a small built-in mapping.

samples.name: stopwatch_cli
samples.description: interactive stopwatch that records lap times
samples.entry_signature: def stopwatch_main() -> None:
steps: Read commands from standard input, one per line: 'start', 'lap', or 'stop'.
On 'start', record the current monotonic time as the start time.
On 'lap', compute the elapsed time since the last lap (or start) and append it to a lap list.
On 'stop', print the total elapsed time and every lap split in order.

samples.name: prime_sieve
samples.description: generates all primes up to N using the Sieve of Eratosthenes
samples.entry_signature: def sieve_main(n: int) -> None:
steps: Read N from the command line.
Initialize a boolean list of size N+1 with all entries True except indices 0 and 1.
For each i from 2 up to sqrt(N), mark every multiple of i greater than i as composite.
Print every index that remains True, separated by spaces.

samples.name: factorize
samples.description: computes the prime factorization of an integer
samples.entry_signature: def factorize_main(n: int) -> None:
steps: Read an integer N from the command line.
For each candidate divisor starting at 2, repeatedly divide N by it while divisible and count the exponent.
Continue with successive integers up to sqrt(remaining N), then include the leftover if it is greater than 1.
Print the factorization as a list of (prime, exponent) pairs.

samples.name: gcd_chain
samples.description: computes the GCD of a list of integers
samples.entry_signature: def gcd_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a list of integers from a file, one per line.
Implement the Euclidean GCD of two integers as a helper.
Reduce the list by applying the two-integer GCD pairwise from left to right.
Print the final GCD.

samples.name: monte_carlo_pi
samples.description: estimates pi using Monte Carlo sampling in the unit square
samples.entry_signature: def mc_pi_main(n_samples: int) -> None:
steps: Read the number of samples N from the command line.
Generate N random (x, y) points uniformly inside the unit square.
Count how many of the points fall inside the quarter-circle of radius 1.
Print the estimate of pi computed from the inside-count ratio.

samples.name: lin_regress
samples.description: fits a simple linear regression to (x, y) data
samples.entry_signature: def regress_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read (x, y) pairs from a file, one pair per line.
Compute the mean of x and of y, and the covariance of x with y and the variance of x.
Compute the slope and intercept of the best-fit line from those quantities.
Print the slope, intercept, and the coefficient of determination R^2.

samples.name: matrix_invert
samples.description: inverts a square matrix using Gauss-Jordan elimination
samples.entry_signature: def invert_main(matrix_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a square matrix from a file with one row per line and numbers separated by spaces.
Augment the matrix with the identity matrix of the same size.
Apply row operations to reduce the left half to the identity, mirroring them on the right half.
Print the right half as the inverse of the input matrix.

samples.name: quadratic_roots
samples.description: finds the real roots of a quadratic ax^2 + bx + c
samples.entry_signature: def quadratic_main(a: float, b: float, c: float) -> None:
steps: Read the coefficients a, b, and c from the command line.
Compute the discriminant b^2 - 4ac.
Decide whether there are zero, one, or two real roots from the sign of the discriminant.
Print the roots in ascending order.

samples.name: fft_radix2
samples.description: computes the DFT of a length-2^k input via a radix-2 FFT
samples.entry_signature: def fft_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read a list of complex numbers from a file, requiring the length to be a power of two.
Apply the bit-reversal permutation to reorder the input list.
Run iterative butterfly operations across log2(N) stages to compute the DFT in place.
Print the resulting frequency-domain coefficients.

samples.name: stats_summary
samples.description: prints summary statistics for one numeric column of a CSV
samples.entry_signature: def stats_main(csv_path: str, column: str) -> None:
steps: Load the CSV into row dictionaries and extract the chosen numeric column as a list of floats.
Compute count, mean, median, standard deviation, and the first and third quartiles.
Identify outliers as values outside [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR].
Print the summary statistics along with the number of outliers.

samples.name: simpsons_rule
samples.description: numerically integrates a hard-coded function via Simpson's rule
samples.entry_signature: def simpsons_main(a: float, b: float, n: int) -> None:
steps: Read the interval endpoints a and b and the number of subintervals N from the command line.
Sample the hard-coded function f at the N+1 equally spaced abscissas across [a, b].
Apply Simpson's rule by combining the samples with weights 1, 4, 2, 4, ..., 4, 1.
Print the approximate integral along with N and the spacing h.

samples.name: binomial_pmf
samples.description: computes the binomial PMF for a set of k values
samples.entry_signature: def binomial_main(n: int, p: float, ks_path: str) -> None:
steps: Read N, p, and a list of k values from the command line and a file.
Implement the binomial coefficient C(n, k) using a multiplicative formula.
For each k, compute the PMF value n_choose_k * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).
Print a table of k, PMF, and the running cumulative probability.

samples.name: eigen_power
samples.description: estimates the dominant eigenvalue of a square matrix by power iteration
samples.entry_signature: def eigen_main(matrix_path: str, n_iter: int) -> None:
steps: Read a square matrix from a file with rows separated by newlines.
Initialize a random unit vector of matching dimension.
For each iteration, multiply the vector by the matrix and renormalize the result.
Print the Rayleigh-quotient eigenvalue estimate at every iteration.

samples.name: fraction_reduce
samples.description: reduces fractions of the form 'a/b' to lowest terms
samples.entry_signature: def fraction_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read fractions formatted as 'a/b' from a file, one per line.
For each fraction, compute the GCD of the numerator and denominator using Euclid's algorithm.
Divide both the numerator and the denominator by the GCD to obtain the reduced form.
Print each reduced fraction in the same 'a/b' format.

samples.name: chinese_remainder
samples.description: solves a system of congruences with the Chinese Remainder Theorem
samples.entry_signature: def crt_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read (a_i, m_i) pairs from a file, one per line.
Verify that the moduli are pairwise coprime by checking GCDs.
Apply the constructive CRT formula to obtain a unique solution modulo the product of moduli.
Print the solution along with the combined modulus.

samples.name: convex_hull
samples.description: computes the convex hull of 2D points via Graham scan
samples.entry_signature: def hull_main(path: str) -> None:
steps: Read 2D points from a file as 'x y' on each line.
Find the lowest point (smallest y, ties broken by x) and use it as the pivot.
Sort the remaining points by polar angle around the pivot.
Build the hull by iterating through the sorted points and maintaining a stack with left-turn checks; print the hull vertices in counter-clockwise order.
